rules.old_rule: Weekly start/sit analysis could implicitly favor nominal NFL starters or projected RB volume in FLEX decisions.
rules.new_rule: Treat JD as a deliberately WR-driven roster. Fill the two mandatory RB slots with the best two evidence-based RB plays each week, then compare FLEX candidates across positions without an RB preference. Strong WR depth should be exploited when full-PPR route/target/air-yard evidence beats an RB's role.
rules.reason: User clarified intended auction construction after Week 2 and the Dobbins-over-Vele miss exposed that the prior process did not sufficiently account for roster construction and full-PPR WR strength.
rules.expected_effect: Better use of Chase/JSN/McMillan plus Wicks/Vele/Douglas/Worthy depth; fewer low-receiving-floor RB FLEX starts.

rules.old_rule: Injury-created available backfield touches could materially elevate an early-down RB even when the replacement distribution and receiving role were uncertain.
rules.new_rule: Do not convert an injury to another RB into assumed consolidated workload. Re-price the whole backfield using snaps, routes, targets, carries, goal-line/red-zone work, two-minute/third-down work, offensive environment and replacement candidates. In full PPR, demonstrated receiving participation can outweigh speculative carry volume.
rules.reason: R.J. Harvey's Week 2 absence did not consolidate Denver around Dobbins; Jonah Coleman remained heavily involved and scored, while Dobbins' receiving floor stayed minimal.
rules.expected_effect: Lower overreaction to injury news and more accurate distributional workload analysis.

rules.old_rule: Nominal depth-chart status and generic consensus RB ranking could retain excessive weight despite poor offensive environment or weak receiving role.
rules.new_rule: For every RB start decision, explicitly score offensive environment and quarterback quality alongside workload. Do not treat touches as equal-quality opportunities. Compare the RB directly with all viable roster alternatives using user-supplied advanced data, current beat/Twitter intelligence, expert consensus, matchup and full-PPR role.
rules.reason: User repeatedly flagged Cleveland/Deshaun Watson as a negative Judkins environment and questioned Dobbins; the Brain did not weight those warnings strongly enough before Week 2.
rules.expected_effect: More complete compare/contrast analysis and fewer starts driven by generic rank or nominal RB1 labels.

rules.old_rule: Dobbins and Judkins remained normal weekly starting candidates absent a specific downgrade.
rules.new_rule: Beginning Week 3, J.K. Dobbins and Quinshon Judkins are BENCH by default. Either may be reconsidered only when new role/usage/environment evidence materially changes the thesis. Braelon Allen receives serious weekly RB2 consideration, but the two RB starters remain evidence-based rather than hard-coded.
rules.reason: Explicit user correction after Week 2; Dobbins' split/receiving limitations and Judkins' Cleveland environment require a reset rather than continuation bias.
rules.expected_effect: Force fresh weekly RB comparison and prevent continuation bias while preserving flexibility if roles change.

adoption_note: These are user-directed structural/process corrections, not hindsight edits to prior decision records. Historical reasoning remains immutable. Formal Week 2 outcome/process grading remains append-only in the decision-learning review path.
